blocks.title: Core Concept
blocks.text:
Introduction
According to 'WHO, ''total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, i.e., physical, emotional, behavioural and social is known as reproductive health''

Reasons for the increase in population:

• Decline in death rate
    • Decline in maternal mortality rate (MMR)
    • Decline in infant mortality rate (IMR)
Increase in the number of people in reproducible age

According to the 2011 census report, the population growth rate was less than 2%, i.e., 20/1000/year.

Measures to check population growth rate:
      • Motivating smaller families by using various contraceptive methods ("Hum Do Hamare Do").
      • Statutory raising of marriageable age of females to 18 years and that of males to 21 years.
      • Incentives are given to couples with smaller families.

Reproductive Health – Problems and Strategies

  • India was among the first countries in the world to initiate action plans and programmes (family planning was initiated in 1951) to attain total reproductive health as a social goal.
  • Improved programmes covering wider reproduction-related areas are currently in operation under the popular name 'Reproductive and child  Health Care (RCH) programmes'

blocks.title: Reproduction Related Aspects
blocks.text:
Reproductive organs, adolescence and related change, safe and hygienic sexual practices, sexually transmitted diseases (STD), AIDS, available birth control options, care of pregnant mothers, post-natal care of the mother and child, the importance of breastfeeding, equal opportunities for the male and the female child, problem due to uncontrolled population growth, social evils like sex abuse and sex-related crimes, etc.

Indications of improved reproductive health of the society:

  • Better awareness about sex-related matters
  • Increased number of medically assisted deliveries and better post-natal care leading to decreased maternal and infant mortality rates
  • Increased number of couples with small families
  • Better detection and cure of STIs
  • Overall increased medical facilities for all sex-related problems, etc.

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text:
1. Lack of Awareness and Misconceptions:

• Misinformation about contraception
• Stigma surrounding sexual health

2 Inadequate Access to Services

• Poor quality of services

3 Government Policies and Program Implementation:

• By addressing these issues and implementing evidence-based strategies, RCH programs can contribute to improving reproductive health outcomes and reducing maternal and child mortality.

blocks.title: Question.1
blocks.question:
Which one of the following was the first country in the world to adopt a family planning programme?

(1) Japan                                                     (2) USA

(3) India                                                      (4) Bangladesh
blocks.answer:
Answer = 3

Explanation:

India was the first country in the world to adopt an official family planning programme in 1952. This program aimed to control population growth and improve maternal and child health. Over the years, the program evolved into a broader Reproductive and Child Health Programme, focusing on contraception, health education, and women's empowerment.
blocks.prompt: Which one of the following was the first country in the world to adopt a family planning programme?

blocks.title: Question.2
blocks.question:
Family planning programmes were initiated in :-

(1) 1947

(2) 1951

(3) 1977

(4) 1955
blocks.answer:
The correct answer is:
(2) 1951

Explanation:

Family planning programmes were officially initiated in India in 1951. This was a part of the country's effort to control its rapidly growing population and improve health outcomes for women and children. The program focused on providing information about contraception and offering birth control methods to the public.

blocks.title: Core Concepts: Amniocentesis
blocks.text:
In the 14th to 16th week of pregnancy, with the help of a long surgical needle, amniotic fluid is taken out from the uterus. In this fluid, few cells of the embryo (skin, liver and placenta) are present.

These cells are tested to know

(i) Genetic disorder/chromosomal abnormalities like Down syndrome.

(ii) Metabolic disorder (deficiency of protein, enzymes, hormones).

(iii) Detection of Sex (Barr bodies).

There is a statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination to legally check increasing female foeticides.

blocks.title: QUESTION.1
blocks.question:
Amniocentesis is:

(1) analysis of the chemical composition of fluids of a pregnant woman

(2) withdrawal of allantoic fluid from pregnant women

(3) done before pregnancy

(4) study of metaphase chromosomes from amniotic fluid to identify chromosomal abnormality
blocks.answer:
Answer = 4

Amniocentesis is a medical procedure that involves taking a sample of amniotic fluid from the sac surrounding the fetus in the uterus. This fluid contains cells from the fetus, which can be used to analyze chromosomes and genetic material. The test is primarily done to identify chromosomal abnormalities like Down syndrome or other genetic conditions.
options: (1) analysis of the chemical composition of fluids of a pregnant woman
(2) withdrawal of allantoic fluid from pregnant women
(4) study of metaphase chromosomes from amniotic fluid to identify chromosomal abnormality

blocks.title: QUESTION.2
blocks.question:
Amniocentesis is used to determine:
(1) length of embryo

(2) size of embryo

(3) hereditary disease of embryo

(4) All of the above
blocks.answer:
Answer = 3

Amniocentesis is primarily used to detect hereditary diseases and genetic disorders in the fetus. By analyzing the chromosomes in the amniotic fluid, doctors can diagnose conditions such as Down syndrome, Cystic fibrosis, or other chromosomal abnormalities.

blocks.title: QUESTION.3
blocks.question:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A: Amniocentesis for sex determination is one of the strategies of the Reproductive and Child Health Care Programme.

Reason R: Ban on amniocentesis checks the increasing menace of female foeticide.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

(1) Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

(2) A is true but R is false.

(3) A is false but R is true.

(4) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
blocks.answer:
Answer = 3

Explanation:

  • Assertion A: Amniocentesis for sex determination is not one of the strategies of the Reproductive and Child Health Care Programme. The Reproductive and Child Health Care Programme focuses on improving maternal and child health, providing contraception, and addressing reproductive health issues. Amniocentesis is not allowed for sex determination because it can lead to the practice of female foeticide.
  • Reason R: Ban on amniocentesis for sex determination is indeed a measure to prevent the increasing menace of female foeticide, a practice where female fetuses are aborted after being identified as female. Laws like the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act prohibit using amniocentesis for sex determination to curb this issue.
options: (1) Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
(2) A is true but R is false.
(3) A is false but R is true.
(4) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

blocks.title: Core Concepts: Contraceptive Methods
blocks.text:
Methods, which help to prevent unwanted pregnancies:

Features of an ideal contraceptive:

  • User-friendly
  • Easily available
  • Effective
  • Reversible with no or least side-effects
  • No interference with sexual drive/desire, and/or sexual act of the user.

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Natural/Traditional methods:

  • Work on the principle of avoiding chances of ovum and sperm meeting
  • Almost nil side effects and high chances of failure
  • Artificial methods:
(1) Barriers methods: In these methods ovum (egg) and sperms are prevented from physically meeting with the help of barriers.

(2) Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs)

  • IUDs are contraceptive devices that are inserted by doctors or expert nurses in the uterus through the vagina.
  • IUDs are an ideal contraceptive for females who want to delay pregnancy or space between children.
  • It is one of the most widely accepted methods of contraception in India.
These IUDs are of the following types:

(3) Hormonal Methods:

These are the  most widely used and most effective methods (almost 100% effective).

In this method oral pills, injections and implants are used.

(ii) Implants & Injections:

Progestogens alone or in combination with estrogen can also be used by females as injections or implants under the skin.

• In these implants/injections, high level of progesterone hormone is present which Inhibit secretion of gonadotropins so ovulation in absent. e.g. Norplant (implant).

EMERGENCY CONTRACEPTIVES

  • Found to be very effective if used within 72 hours of coitus.
  • Used to avoid possible pregnancy due to rape or unprotected intercourse.
  • It includes Progestogens or progestogen - Estrogen combination or IUD's.

blocks.title: Surgical methods/Sterilization/Terminal method
blocks.text:
Surgical methods are generally advised for the male/female partner as a terminal method to prevent any more pregnancies.

  • Surgical intervention blocks gamete transport and thereby prevents conception.
  • Sterilization procedure in the male is called vasectomy, and that in the female is tubectomy.
  • In vasectomy , a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum.
  • Whereas in tubectomy, a small  part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up through a small incision in the abdomen or through vagina.
SIDE EFFECTS OF CONTRACEPTIVES

  • Nausea
  • Abdominal pain
  • Breakthrough bleeding
  • Irregular menstrual bleeding
  • Even breast cancer through not very significant should not be totally ignored.

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Medical Termination of Pregnancy (M.T.P):
    • Induced abortion / Intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full-term.
    • It was legalised by the government of India in 1971 with some strict conditions to avoid its misuse.
    • Relatively safe during first trimester (up to 12 weeks of pregnancy)
    • Much more risky during second trimester
MTP is performed to get rid of unwanted pregnancies due to:

  • Casual unprotected intercourse
  • Failure of contraceptive used during coitus
  • Rape
  • In cases where continuation of the pregnancy could be harmful or even fatal to the mother or to the foetus or both.

blocks.title: Core Concepts- Sexually Transmitted Infections(STIs)
blocks.text:
Also known as Venereal Diseases (VDs) or Reproductive Tract Infections (RTIs), e.g.:

1. Gonorrhoea

2. Syphilis

3. Genital herpes

4. Chlamydiasis

5. Genital warts

6. Trichomoniasis

7. Hepatitis- B

8. HIV

  • Some of the infections like this Hepatitis B and AIDS can also be transmitted by sharing injection needles, surgical instruments, etc., with infected persons.
  • Except for hepatitis B, genital herpes and HIV infections, other diseases are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.
  • The most vulnerable age group for STIs is 15 to 24 years.
For prevention of STIs:

  • Avoid sex with unknown partners / multiple partners
  • Always try to use condoms during coitus
  • In case of doubt, go to a qualified doctor for early detection and get complete treatment if diagnosed with an infection.

blocks.title: Core Concepts: Infertility
blocks.text:
Infertility

Inability to produce children in spite of unprotected sexual cohabitation. In India, often, the female is blamed for the couple being childless, but more often than not, the problem lies in the male partner.

Possible reasons:

  • Physical
  • Congenital
  • Diseases
  • Drugs
  • Immunological
  • Psychological

blocks.title: Question.1
blocks.question:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) is another specialised procedure of in-vivo fertilisation.

Statement II: Infertility cases due to the inability of the male partner to inseminate the female can be corrected by artificial insemination (AI).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

(1) Statement I is correct but statement II is false

(2) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true

(3) Both Statement I and Statement II are true

(4) Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
blocks.answer:
Answer = 2

Explanation:

  • Statement I: Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) is a specialized procedure used in in-vitro fertilization (IVF), but not in in-vivo fertilization. In ICSI, a single sperm is directly injected into an egg to facilitate fertilization, which is part of IVF, an artificial reproductive technique. Therefore, this statement is incorrect because ICSI is part of in-vitro, not in-vivo fertilization.
  • Statement II: Artificial insemination (AI) is a procedure used to treat infertility when the male partner is unable to inseminate the female due to various factors (e.g., low sperm count, poor sperm motility). This statement is true, as AI involves introducing sperm into the female reproductive tract by means other than sexual intercourse.
options: (1) Statement I is correct but statement II is false
(2) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
(3) Both Statement I and Statement II are true
(4) Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

blocks.title: Question.2
blocks.question:
In the case of a couple where the male has a very low sperm count, which technique will be suitable for fertilisation?

(1) Gamete intracytoplasmic fallopian transfer

(2) Artificial Insemination

(3) Intracytoplasmic sperm injection

(4) Intrauterine transfer
blocks.answer:
Answer = 2

Explanation:

When the male has a very low sperm count, the best technique for fertilization is Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI). In ICSI, a single sperm is directly injected into the egg, bypassing the need for large numbers of sperm. This method is particularly useful for cases of male infertility due to low sperm count or poor sperm motility.
blocks.prompt: In the case of a couple where the male has a very low sperm count, which technique will be suitable for fertilisation?

blocks.title: Question.3
blocks.question:
Full form of MTP with respect to reproductive health is:-

(1) Maternal termination of pregnancy

(2) Mid-term pregnancy

(3) Medical try for pregnancy

(4) Medical termination of pregnancy
blocks.answer:
Answer = 4

Explanation:

  • MTP refers to Medical Termination of Pregnancy, which is the process of intentionally ending a pregnancy through medical or surgical means.
  • It is often done to protect the health of the mother, in cases of fetal abnormalities, or in pregnancies resulting from rape or contraceptive failure.
  • In India, MTP is regulated by the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971, and it allows abortion under specific conditions up to a certain gestational period.
blocks.prompt: Full form of MTP with respect to reproductive health is:-

blocks.title: Question.4
blocks.question:
Which of the following sexually transmitted infections are completely curable?

(1) HIV infection and Trichomoniasis

(2) Syphilis and trichomoniasis

(3) Hepatitis – B and Genital herpes

(4) Genital herpes and Genital warts
blocks.answer:
Answer = 2

Explanation:

  • Syphilis: A bacterial infection caused by Treponema pallidum. It is completely curable with the use of antibiotics such as penicillin if detected early.
  • Trichomoniasis: A parasitic infection caused by Trichomonas vaginalis. It is also completely curable with medications like metronidazole or tinidazole.
blocks.prompt: Which of the following sexually transmitted infections are completely curable?
